chunks: From him and Ahmad together, from Ibn Mahbub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Ammar al-Sabati, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Every Muslim, among Muslims, who apostatizes from Islam and denies Muhammad's (peace be upon him and his family) prophethood and rejects it, then his blood is permissible for anyone who hears that from him, and his wife is separated from him on the day he apostatizes, so do not approach her, and his wealth is distributed among his heirs, and his wife observes the waiting period of the one whose husband died, and it is upon the Imam to kill him and not ask him for repentance.

key_terms.عِدَّةَ الْمُتَوَفَّى: The waiting period of the deceased

ai.seo_question: What are the specific legal consequences for a Muslim who apostatizes and denies the prophethood of Muhammad according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-istibsar articulates the Shia juristic view of 'immediate apostasy' (al-ridda al-fouri) by specifying the denial of Muhammad’s prophethood as the trigger for distinct legal consequences. It highlights the Imam’s authority to execute the apostate without the usual waiting period for repentance (istitab), while simultaneously establishing that the wife’s separation is immediate and her waiting period (iddah) mirrors that of a widow, reflecting a unique status in Shia fiqh.
